correctness.rationale: For every n>=3, the omitted-vertex gap proof gives equivalence to a finite cyclic adjacency rule (short gaps 0/1 alternate with >=2, and gaps 3/4 have short neighbors). Deleting one selected vertex exactly splits a gap. This proves a necessary/sufficient inclusion-minimality condition. A 3-state transfer matrix has determinant D(x,z), and the rooted-cycle multiplier n/k yields -xD_x/D. The equality-rigidity and residue corrections follow from 5n-7|S|=3(t-h)+2s_0+2c_3+c_2 and explicit extensible witnesses. The original graph-definition verifier examined all 1,048,568 vertex subsets over n=3..19; coefficient and spectrum checks extend to n=154. Finite checks corroborate the complete elementary proof; no computational extrapolation is used.

value.rationale: The established graph invariant is a maximum over inclusion-minimal super dominating sets, intrinsically distinct from the well-studied minimum number and ordinary all-set counts. An exact full cardinality polynomial, a structural five-gap language, two sharp residue corrections to the 5n/7 upper size and seven extremals at every multiple of seven provide complete, nonroutine enumerative and structural information for a canonical infinite family. The proof supplies reusable finite-state/gap machinery, without asserting downstream results.
